result.dimension: schema / services.yaml / strings.json / translations consistency for raw_pymammotion_step_response_probe

findings.title: UI-visible linear_speed description calls the 300 speed "measured" when the code says no such measurement exists
findings.summary: strings.json:2512 and translations/en.json:2512 read "Measured and not linear: 400 is about 0.26 m/s, 300 about 0.16 m/s", but services.py:9549-9551 states "There is NO sustained-speed measurement at 300 at all; 0.10 is a deliberately pessimistic floor under an extrapolated ~0.16 m/s", and the probe's own runtime caveat (services.py:10146-10150) tells the operator "typical_speed_m_s at linear 300 is EXTRAPOLATED -- no sustained speed has ever been measured at 300. Treat any 300 projection as an estimate, not a measurement." The description strips exactly the provenance the response payload is careful to attach. HA resolves service field descriptions from translations in preference to services.yaml, so this is the text the operator actually sees in Developer Tools.
findings.failure_scenario: Planning the first-ever linear-300 run, the operator reads "Measured ... 300 about 0.16 m/s" in the service form and sizes step_ms/max_travel_m from it as if 300 were a characterised operating point (23 s x 0.16 = 3.68 m, so max_travel_m 4.0 "with margin"). The 0.16 figure is a single 1.37x ramp/sustained ratio transplanted from linear 400 onto one 4 s ramp-inclusive sample at 300; nothing bounds the error. If 300 in fact sustains faster, the window ends on the travel guard mid-step and censors 2a -- the exact wasted-supervised-run outcome step_window_travel_exceeds_budget and travel_projection were added to prevent -- and the run record will say the config was chosen from a "measured" speed that was never measured.

findings.title: services.yaml quotes 0.12 m/s for linear 300, contradicting strings.json (0.16) and the code's own projection table
findings.summary: services.yaml:875-876 reads "Measured, and NOT linear: 400 is ~0.26 m/s, 300 is ~0.12 m/s" for the same field whose strings.json/en.json description says "400 is about 0.26 m/s, 300 about 0.16 m/s", and whose in-code projection uses _STEP_RESPONSE_TYPICAL_SPEED_BY_LINEAR = {300: 0.16, 400: 0.216} (services.py:9560). 0.12 is the ramp-inclusive 4 s average (0.116 m/s, services.py:9548-9549), while the paired 0.26 for 400 is a full-window sustained rate -- two different metrics presented as one comparison, which is the error the repo's own "ramp-inclusive averages understate sustained by 1.37x" note exists to prevent. Commit 29b810bf corrected the strings.json/en.json copy of this field and left services.yaml untouched, so the two now disagree by 33%. It also makes the "NOT linear" claim itself wrong-sized: 0.26 vs 0.12 reads as a 54% speed cut for a 25% command cut, where like-for-like it is 39%.
findings.failure_scenario: A session sizing the intended long/slow run reads services.yaml (the file it greps, since the service is invoked from YAML not the UI form), computes a 23 s window at 0.12 m/s = 2.76 m, and sets max_travel_m = 3.0 believing it holds 0.24 m of headroom. The service's own travel_projection computes 0.16 x 23 = 3.68 m and returns likely_guard_trip: true -- the dry run contradicts the plan the operator arrived with, and if the flag is skimmed past the run trips the guard mid-step and censors the measurement it was spent on.

findings.title: select selector options are strings while default/example are integers, so the dropdown has no preselected value
findings.summary: linear_speed (services.yaml:878-884) declares default: 400 and example: 400 as integers against select options "300"/"400"; step_angular_speed (services.yaml:887-895) does the same with default: 120 against "-180"/"-120"/"120"/"180". Every other select selector in this 67-service file quotes its default to match its options (start_mow.border_mode default '0', ultra_wave '2', channel_mode '0', rain_tactics '1', toward_mode '0', mowing_laps '1', obstacle_laps '1'), so these two are the only mismatches in the file. The dispatch path is unaffected -- I executed STEP_RESPONSE_PROBE_SCHEMA against "300"/"400" and "-180"/"120": vol.Coerce(int) + vol.In(...) accepts the frontend's strings, the ints, and string numbers for every other field -- but the HA select widget matches its value against the option list by identity, so the integer 400 matches no option.
findings.failure_scenario: The operator opens raw_pymammotion_step_response_probe in Developer Tools -> Actions and enables the optional Linear speed field. The dropdown renders with nothing selected even though services.yaml declares default: 400, so the operator either concludes the field has no default and picks a value they did not intend (300 is now one click away from 400 on this open-loop curved drive), or leaves it blank and relies on the schema default without the form confirming it. Quoting the two defaults and examples resolves it.

findings.title: step_ms is documented as "up to 15000 ms" with no mention of the 23 s total-window cap that can refuse it
findings.summary: services.yaml:908 and strings.json:2524 both say step_ms goes "Up to 15000 ms" and name only step_window_travel_exceeds_budget as the pre-dispatch refusal. The three phase selectors permit 5000 + 15000 + 6000 = 26000 ms, but services.py:10114-10115 refuses any total over _STEP_RESPONSE_MAX_TOTAL_MS = 23000 with the bare blocker step_window_too_long, appended straight to the blockers list with no gate detail (unlike every entry from _step_response_gates, which carries a "detail" string). That cap appears nowhere in services.yaml, strings.json, or any translation.
findings.failure_scenario: The operator wants the longest possible step and sets baseline_ms 5000 / step_ms 15000 / settle_ms 6000 -- each inside its own selector range and inside the documented "up to 15000 ms". The dry run comes back would_send: false with blockers ['step_window_too_long'], a name with no detail field and no occurrence anywhere in the service documentation, so the operator has to read services.py to learn that baseline + step + settle must total <= 23000 and which phase to shorten.

findings.title: No services.yaml/strings.json parity test for this service, though continuous_motion_window has one
findings.summary: tests/components/mammotion/test_step_response_probe.py pins the voluptuous schema thoroughly (defaults, the 15000 ceiling, the 4.5 travel cap, the 23 s total, the min-speed table against banked runs) but never opens services.yaml or strings.json. test_continuous_motion_window.py:157, test_arc_probe.py:93 and test_probe_travel_guard.py:298 each do exactly that for their own service, with the comment "A field present in one and not the others has bitten this project before." The AST sweep in test_map_task_visibility.py does cover this service (confirmed: the parametrised id raw_pymammotion_step_response_probe collects and passes), but it only checks that every call.data[...] read resolves from the schema -- it never reads services.yaml, so it cannot see a bound or default drifting between the two files.
findings.failure_scenario: The drift this test class exists to catch is live in the tree right now (findings above: services.yaml says 0.12 m/s, strings.json says 0.16) and shipped with 1003 tests green -- as did beta96's "Fixed at the measured value 400" prose after linear_speed became a two-option select. The next bound change repeats it: raising step_ms in services.yaml to 20000 without touching vol.Range(min=1000, max=15000), or vice versa, ships a UI offering a value the schema rejects (or hiding one it accepts) with a fully green suite, and is discovered only when a supervised run is refused at dispatch time.

result.notes:
VERIFIED CLEAN (no defect): services.yaml parses (67 services, yaml.safe_load). All 16 fields of raw_pymammotion_step_response_probe match STEP_RESPONSE_PROBE_SCHEMA exactly in both directions -- no field in one and not the other, and required/default/selector-bounds agree field by field, checked programmatically against the imported schema object: entity_id/route_start/corridor_polygon required in both; linear_speed 400, step_angular_speed 120, baseline_ms 3000 (1000-5000), step_ms 3000 (1000-15000), settle_ms 4000 (1000-6000), motion_refresh_interval_ms 200 (50-1000), sample_interval_ms 100 (50-1000), max_travel_m 2.50 (0.10-4.5), prefer_ble/dry_run true, three confirms false. max_travel_m's 4.5 ceiling is intact in both.

Select coercion works as HA delivers it -- executed the real schema: {"linear_speed": "300", "step_angular_speed": "-180"} validates to ints 300/-180; ints pass unchanged; string numbers for the ms/float fields coerce correctly. vol.Coerce(int) runs before vol.In, so the string options are never compared against the int membership list.

AST sweep coverage confirmed: pytest --collect-only shows test_handler_read_keys_resolve_from_schema_defaults[raw_pymammotion_step_response_probe]; the sweep unwraps _wrap_exclusive_manual_motion (which this service uses) to reach handle_step_response_probe, and all 16 keys the handler reads resolve. 59 sweep tests pass.

Translations: strings.json and translations/en.json are byte-identical for this service (all 16 fields). The other 11 locales omit it -- consistent with 21 other services absent from strings.json entirely and 25-vs-46 service coverage across every non-en locale; a pre-existing repo convention for raw_*/diagnostic services, not reported. Select option labels are untranslated for this service, as they are for all 24 select selectors in the file.

No stale beta88/beta96 numbers survive in the user-facing files: greps for 7000, 16000, 0.24 and "Fixed at the measured value" return nothing in services.yaml, strings.json, en.json or the card.
